title: “I Want to Work With President Sheinbaum,” Mamdani Says; He Praises Her Policies
author: Redacción/SinEmbargo
content:
_This article originally appeared in the[September 20, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4873706/quiero-trabajar-con-la-
presidenta-sheinbaum-dice-mamdani-elogia-sus-politicas/), a Mexican
independent digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, September 20 (SinEmbargo).—** New York City Mayor Zohran
Mamdani on Sunday recognized the work of President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo to
advance public policies that provide dignified conditions for the population.
In addition, the progressive politician announced his intention to work with
the Mexican head of state in order to promote avenues that mitigate the cost
of living.

> I want to work with President Sheinbaum, as well as with other leaders
> throughout Mexico… recognizing that the crises we face are global crises.
>
> Zohran Mamdani, Mayor of New York City

The New York official made the remarks during his participation in the Urban
20 2026 forum.

During his remarks, Mamdani referred to the impact of housing problems in
Mexico, particularly in Mexico City, where he referenced areas such as the
Colonia Roma neighborhood.

![Claudia Sheinbaum and Clara Brugada](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/02-sheinbaum-brugada.jpg)Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo and
Clara Brugada Molina, two progressive reference points for the New York mayor.
Photo: Moisés Pablo, Cuartoscuro

The mayor stated that he has watched **" with admiration the initiatives of
President Sheinbaum and the ways in which she is addressing the same cost-of-
living problems and the importance and need for dignity in work."**

The Democratic leader of one of the most important financial cities in the
world said that the Mexican capital is an international **" inspiration"**
"because of the way it has responded to the care crisis in our economy."

He also recognized the social work of the Head of Government of Mexico City,
Clara Brugada Molina, who throughout her administration has devoted herself to
implementing policies in favor of culture, sports, recreation, and the
education of the city's residents.

> [Post by @ClaraBrugadaM on
> X](https://twitter.com/ClaraBrugadaM/status/2101706570908172368)

The official explicitly referred to the **Utopías** that the Mexico City
leader has installed around the city, maintaining that this social project
shows "a way to guarantee the dignity of working people and ensure that they
can live a full life."

In that vein, he described it as "a pleasure" to have the participation of
Brugada, "who understands that the problems of the working class must be at
the forefront of politics."

Mamdani was accompanied by the Head of Government of Mexico City, Clara
Brugada, during a conference in which she also referred to the public policies
developed in the Mexican capital.

For her part, the Mexico City leader noted that for decades **neoliberalism
marked the abandonment of national housing policy**. In her words, housing was
understood as a commodity subject to speculation, and it was assumed that only
those with the ability to pay could access it.

> The government stopped building. The only way to access a home was to go
> into debt for life, and millions were also excluded from the traditional
> financial system.
>
> Clara Brugada Molina, Head of Government of Mexico City

Nevertheless, she explained that Mexico City has spent **30 years in a process
of transformation** and that it now has a different housing policy, with a
model that includes the participation of social movements and authorities in
the sector.
